complete_examples.text: In this example, the ΔS is 0.03 m, the Nw is 7, and the Nyquist frequency fN (spatial frequency) and cutoff frequency fC (spatial frequency) are 16.667 (1/m) and 0.1302 (1/m), respectively.

According to the relationship “wavelength (m) = 1/spatial frequency (1/m)”, the wavelength of frequency 0.0299 (1/m) is 33.4 m, and this wavelength can be approximately equivalent to twice the distance between the front and rear bogies (17.5 m), hence, the linear superposition of two bogies’ irregularities exists a phase difference of half a period and occurs the antiresonance phenomenon so that the amplitude of 0.0299 (1/m) spatial frequency is lower than that of other frequencies.
Only one characteristic spatial frequency is considered for easy observation.
Then, the set of PSD values at each spatial frequency is given by qu = (qu(1), qu(2), ..., qu(n)) .
